standard.title: Contribute to discussions with diverse views
standard.description: contribute to discussions that involve diverse views to negotiate outcomes, address issues and compare cultural experiences
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can plan, transact and negotiate with peers and produce bilingual community resources (AC9LCH8EC02). They have collaborated on cultural events and community-facing projects. They have not yet led or facilitated live or online events for community audiences, contributed to sister school negotiations, or produced bilingual community initiatives on social issues.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students contribute to discussions involving diverse views — including facilitating events, negotiating with diverse community stakeholders, collaborating on community initiatives, and addressing social issues in group contexts.

nodes.label: Facilitating and contributing to group discussions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can contribute productively to group discussions with diverse views — facilitating equitable participation, reaching agreement, and managing competing perspectives.
nodes.minimum_width: Contribute to a group discussion using at least two facilitation or negotiation strategies to support equitable participation and move toward a shared outcome.
nodes.typical_width: Plan and facilitate live or online events; collaborate to reach agreement by equally contributing ideas; facilitate student-led activities; contribute to collaborative reports and articles on social issues; negotiate and justify decisions with diverse peers.
wider: Lead a discussion where views conflict — facilitate negotiation and bring the group to a productive outcome using target language

Compare group discussion facilitation conventions in the target language community with Australian school contexts — identify cultural differences in how participation, turn-taking and consensus-building are managed
nodes.hinge_reason: Group discussion facilitation is the prerequisite for all community-facing collaborative activity. Students who can only contribute without facilitating cannot lead the community events and collaborative productions this descriptor requires.

response_modes.reason: Facilitation requires students to manage group dynamics explicitly — ensuring inclusion, managing conflict, building consensus. Explicit facilitation strategy instruction followed by practice in genuinely diverse discussion contexts builds this capacity.

success_criteria: Uses at least two facilitation or negotiation strategies during a group discussion
Helps move the group toward a shared outcome

nodes.label: Community initiatives and sister school connections
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can collaborate on bilingual community initiatives — road safety, sustainability, local activities — and negotiate with potential sister school or Chinese-speaking community connections.
nodes.minimum_width: Contribute to at least one bilingual community initiative or sister school negotiation, producing at least one collaborative output in target language.
nodes.typical_width: Use collaborative tools to produce bilingual versions of community initiatives; negotiate possible sister schools; consider aspects of educational systems across Chinese-speaking regions; participate in virtual exchanges involving bookings and travel negotiations; promote inclusive community activities.
wider: Lead a bilingual community initiative — coordinating the planning, production and delivery of a community-facing bilingual resource
Research and compare possible sister school partners — evaluate candidates using agreed criteria and present a justified recommendation

response_modes.reason: Community initiative collaboration requires students to operate across varied contexts — online platforms, community organisations, school partnerships. Exposure to varied collaboration contexts builds the flexible community engagement capacity the descriptor requires.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Background language learner entry students often have existing connections to target language communities. Width investment here leverages these real connections — turning personal community ties into authentic collaborative projects with genuine communicative purpose.
success_criteria: Contributes to a bilingual community initiative or sister school negotiation
Produces at least one collaborative output in target language

nodes.label: Addressing social issues in group contexts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can contribute to discussions about social issues — presenting balanced views, supporting positions with evidence, and collaboratively writing group reports or articles.
nodes.minimum_width: Contribute to a group discussion or report on a social issue, presenting at least one position supported by evidence and acknowledging at least one alternative view.
nodes.typical_width: Contribute to discussions about social issues with balanced views and supporting evidence; collaboratively write reports and articles on topics such as employment, education or community life; evaluate and provide feedback on peers' contributions; create multimodal resources for various audiences.
wider: Lead a group report on a social issue — coordinating contributions, synthesising diverse views, and producing a balanced, evidence-based group outcome
Compare how social issues are discussed and reported in target language media versus Australian English media — identify differences in framing, evidence use and perspective

response_modes.reason: Social issue discussion integrates facilitation skills (node 1) and community initiative experience (node 2) into a full evidence-based collaborative production. The teaching investment is in creating genuine social issues — real topics of relevance — that require authentic engagement rather than simulated debate.

success_criteria: Contributes a position supported by evidence to a group discussion or report on a social issue
Acknowledges at least one alternative view in the contribution
